answer: activate is one Operational-mode command with several targets: activate-file; swimage (activates the currently installable image, implies a system restart; db-action auto|empty-db|upgrade-db|rollback, default auto); database (activates the currently inactive database, restart-type cold|warm default cold, sanity-check-override false|true default false, checks NE name, shelf serial number and software version); location-led (target chassis or card, led-mode flash|solid default flash, timeout 0..120 s default 0 meaning no timeout); eqpt-fw (resource plus fw-image-name); krp (installs a key replacement package); otdr and otdr-fiber-check; loopback (WSS loopback on an NMC). Unless -f is given the user must confirm. For database snapshots there is a separate command: activate-snapshot db-instance <string> db-paraphrase <string> [sanity-check-override <true|false>], with the pre-condition that a snapshot was taken (take-snapshot).

show capabilities-<name> is the per-card one: name is the card name and it retrieves that card's capabilities. show l0-capabilities is the photonic one: it takes no parameters and shows the capability details related to the node's Layer 0 functions. show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs] is the add/drop one: max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees (20, uint8; 0 if not supported, degrees exist only on OADM node types, ILA is 0 by convention because it has two fixed directions) and max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups (110, uint8; also OADM-only). Note that max-degrees is the maximum working degree-number, not necessarily the supported deployment configuration. All three are show-only and run in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode.

show controller-card-<name> displays only the controller: redundancy-status active|standby|not-in-service (default not-in-service), redundancy-standby-status ready-synchronized|not-ready-synchronizing|not-ready-synchronize-fail|lock-out|card-not-present (default not-ready-synchronizing), number-of-switchover-events and time-of-last-switchover (both visible only on the active controller), and additional-details (string 0..128). show card-<name> is the card-base object common to all card types: required-type, required-subtype, card-mode, category, chassis-name/slot-name/subslot-name, power-profile, max-power-draw, last-reboot-reason, last-reboot-time, admin-state lock|maintenance|unlock (default unlock), oper-state, avail-state. show supported-card-<card-type> is the per-model capability table: supported-subtype, default-card-mode, supported-card-mode, card-width, card-height, category, grid-mode-support, max-power-draw, location-led-support, console-port-support, support-serdes-config, supported-bands, supported-features.

macsec-entity is the Ethernet MACsec object: add macsec-entity-<name> supporting-facility (for example ethernet-6-3-3), enabled default true, link-security-control must-secure|should-secure (default must-secure), replay-protection enable|disable, replay-protection-window 0..4294967295 (default 0). Its cipher is not configured here; it is read back as negotiated-cipher-suite and chosen through mka-policy macsec-cipher-suite. secure-entity is the optical/L1 encryption object: add secure-entity-<name> supporting-facility (optical-carrier, odu or OTUflex) plus remote-secure-entity, enabled default false, re-key-frequency 3600..86400 s (default 28800), re-key-fail-policy kill-traffic|continue-traffic (default continue-traffic), traffic-kill-offset 0..86400 s (default 0). Its cipher terms live in the read-only secure-entity-sa-proposal: encryption-algorithm aes-gcm-16, encryption-key-length key-length-256, integrity-algorithm none, dh-group ecp-521.

ase-idler-service is the ASE idler filling function on a card (add/delete/set/show): ase-idler-enable enabled|disabled, default disabled, turns ASE filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum; ase-idler-state reports ase-enabled, ase-partially-enabled, ase-faulted or ase-disabled (default ase-disabled); function is idler; alarm-report-control default allowed. ase-idler-source is the ASE pump that produces the signal (set/show only): pump-enable enabled|disabled default disabled, pump-state, target-output-power range -3.00..20.50 dBm default 13, admin-state lock|unlock|maintenance default unlock, function ase-idler-source, with supporting-input-port and supporting-output-port. sw-service does not belong with them: show sw-service-<sv-name> or show sw-services lists the software services and containers on the node, with state off|ok|fail, state-details, cpu-usage, memory-usage, uptime, last-start-time and reboot-count.

No, they are not harmless. change-ztp-mode [-f] [ztp-mode=]<enabled|disabled> toggles Zero Touch Provisioning: change-ztp-mode enabled starts ZTP, reverts the database to the factory default and triggers a system reboot; change-ztp-mode disabled disables ZTP and stops it if it is already running. Current mode is read with show ztp. clear [-f] recover-mode clears the recover-mode flag, which confirms the current configuration as-is, re-enables communication with the line cards and potentially reconfigures traffic settings, so it may be traffic impacting; it has no parameters. Both are Operational mode and prompt for confirmation unless -f is given. The carrier-mode commands are read-only by comparison: show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> and show supported-carrier-mode-<name>/<carrier-mode> only display capacity, client-mode, baud-rate, application, compatibility-id, status and supported-subtypes.

State: show third-party-app-<app-name> gives state running|stopped|failed (default stopped) and enable true|false (default false; when enabled the app is started, including after a system restart), plus version, vendor, product and information; show third-party-app-info-<location-id>/<app-name> gives version, state and information per location. Firmware side: show third-party-fw-<fw-name> gives file-status valid|invalid|missing, path, version, crc, vendor, part-number, nsa-upgrade-version, present-in-eqpt and applicable-eqpt (max 80 elements each). Clearing: clear [-f] app [app-name=]<value> clears third party apps. To act on a stuck app without clearing it, use appctl [app-name=] [command=]restart|netls|exec [[target=]] [[parameters=]]; target defaults to system, and parameters apply to restart or exec (max 50 elements).

Per-session is cli-session-config: set cli-session-config-<session-id> cli-lines <value> where cli-lines is the number of rows before pausing, range 10..1000, default 40; also cli-columns 80..4000 default 80, interactive-mode true|false default true (set per CLI session and not persistent), and display-timestamp default false. The protocol as a whole is cli: enabled default true (it cannot be disabled from within a CLI session), port 1..65535 default 22, script-dir, default-interactive-mode default true (affects only newly created sessions), and show-alarm-columns default default-columns, which has global effect on all CLI sessions. The two system configuration objects are config (show config [<entity-id>|<entity-type>], displays non-default configuration recursively from the current scope) and extended-config (add/delete/show extended-config-<name>, a non-standard configuration that introduces exceptional behaviour globally; the name must match one known by the system).

set is the generic attribute assignment: set [-f|-v] [<entity id>] <attribute> <value> [<attribute> <value> ...] [<filter> ...], at least one attribute-value pair, all belonging to the same managed entity; it supports wildcards (card-*, port-1-4-*, port-1-*-3), ranges card-1-[1..4] and lists, and asks for confirmation when the request may have traffic impact or implicitly affects multiple instances. set-alarm-state is a separate operation: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>...) changes the operator state of alarms, with states none, ack and close, from 1 up to 10 alarm-ids, and acknowledge-text 0..256 characters. set-time [new-time=]<value> changes the system time and is only applicable when the time-source is manual (NTP not enabled), using ISO 8601 form 2017-01-12T10:22:25Z or an offset such as +03:00. The one ending in -set is unrelated: named-value-set-<db-entry-name>/<named-value-set-name> value <string 1..1024>.

mc is the Media Channel, a spectrum slot on an OMS: add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value> in MHz; center-frequency and slot-width (upper minus lower) are computed by the system; auto-delete default disabled; the referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, not an ADG. nmc is the Network Media Channel, the per-carrier channel whose parent-facility can be a Media Channel or an OMS: add nmc-<name> parent-facility <value> center-frequency <190650000..196700000 MHz> [width 15000..200000 MHz, default 35000, configured as the 3 dB bandwidth matching the transponder baud rate], plus power, attenuation and ASE-insertion attributes. The fillers occupy unused spectrum and are system-created: mc-f is show-only (lower-frequency, upper-frequency, slot-width) and nmc-f is show plus set of admin-state and alarm-report-control, reporting alloc- and actual- lower/upper-frequency and bandwidth (alloc-bandwidth default 75000 MHz) and power-actual-tx/rx.

The scan is run by activate otdr [entity=]<port> [[otdr-file-prefix=]<value>], or activate otdr-fiber-check [entity=]<ots-r-id> for a manual OTDR-based fiber check (up to 3 tests; it returns an error if a manual scan or automatic Raman fiber check is already in progress). Tuning lives in otdr-ptp: otdr-range auto or 0..300.0 km (set it to fiber length plus 10 percent), otdr-pulse-width auto or 10..20000 ns, otdr-measurement-speed fast|medium|slow|precision|auto|high-precision, otdr-ior auto or 1.0..2.0, otdr-fiber-type (auto, SSMF, SMF-ULL, LEAF and others), otdr-resolution auto or 0.4..100.0, peak-power auto or 5..14.5, launching-fiber-length 0..50 m (default 0, auto not supported). The answer comes out of otdr-ptp: otdr-fiber-break-distance in km, or not-available if no break was identified, plus otdr-last-measurement and the generated .sor file in otdr-last-measurement-file. Progress is in otdr: otdr-state not-available|idle|measuring|finished|fail, otdr-measurement-time, otdr-measurement-port, otdr-measurement-direction and otdr-error.

Each dns-server entry carries origin: dhcp means the address was assigned to the system by a DHCP server, manual means it was configured by hand (default manual). An entry that keeps coming back after deletion is being re-supplied by DHCP; convert it with set dns-server-<address> origin manual. Whether DHCP values are taken at all is decided by dns assignment-method manual|dhcp|both, default both, alongside dns enabled true|false (default true) and dns search (suffix, must contain at least one dot, 0..64). For the relay there are two levels: the global dhcp-relay with mode disabled|ipv4|ipv6 (default disabled) and server-address (at least one IP must be configured when enabled), and the per-interface if-dhcp-relay-<if-name> dhcp-relay-enabled true|false, default false, which enables the function on that interface and obeys the global dhcp-relay settings. A relay that does nothing is usually mode disabled or dhcp-relay-enabled still false.

clear [-f] system [type=]<value> [[target=]<value>] [[restart-behavior=]<value>] does the secure wipe, with three types. factory-reset resets the system or a specific chassis/card to factory configuration, stopping target traffic services and removing the respective files and user configurations; it does not take effect for G30 OCC2T/OCC2E but is supported for the G30 FRCU controller. full-wipe cleans the entire system and reinstalls the software on controller and line cards, removing all files, configurations and software, and recovery then requires a base software reinstall from ONIE. inactive only clears the inactive software partition. target defaults to the whole system; restart-behavior is a standard restart (default) or shutdown, and shutdown is not supported on the L0 cards. If you want to keep logs and PM data, use clear [-f] database instead (clear-type full, keep-networking or initialize-from-script): it resets the database and reboots, and the guide states it does not wipe logs, PM data or other non-configuration data.

show unprovisioned-inventory-<chassis-serial-number>/<slot-name> lists inventory that has been detected but not yet accepted by the Node Controller in a multi-chassis configuration; it reports actual-type, actual-subtype, hardware-version, sw-support-revision, PON, serial-number, clei, vendor, part-number, manufacture-date and detection-timestamp, the last time the Node Controller detected that unprovisioned equipment. show nct-connection-<src-port>/<dst-port> shows the NCT links the system filled in dynamically, with src-chassis, dst-chassis and src-chassis-state/dst-chassis-state of node controller, provisioned or unprovisioned; ports on an unprovisioned chassis appear as <chassis-serial-number>-<slot>-NCT-<id>. Once the shelf is added, show chassis-<name> gives is-node-controller, chassis-role unknown|main-chassis|sub-chassis, expected-serial-number (which informs the NC of a sub-chassis serial number) and equipment-discovery-ready, which stays false until all equipment was discovered at startup.

The deciding attribute is amplifier control-mode: auto-max-pw (default), where the system sets the gain automatically targeting maximum output power, or manual, where you set gain-target yourself in the range 0..40 dB (default 0.0). amp-control-support tells you whether auto is even possible on that card: auto means both manual and auto-max-pw are supported, manual-only means only manual. gain-range-control follows control-mode automatically (manual with manual, auto with auto-max-pw), with gain-range-target standard|low|high; in auto mode use gain-adjustment [-20.00..20.00] dB, supported only where function is pa or inline. Nothing comes out if amplifier-enable is disabled (the default), if forced-shutdown is true, if admin-state is lock, or after an input OLOS shutdown once olos-shutdown-soak-timer (0..2000 ms) expires, unless olos-shutdown-disable is true. Output also depends on the OSC signal for node-type ILA, or on the OMS facilities and an OXcon for node-type OADM. Read back gain-operating, pump-state, output-power-mon and control-state.

show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> tells you which member is live: state is active, standby, available or unknown, with role working or protection and transport-entity giving the underlying facility. At group level, show protection-group-<name> pg-state reports no-request, forced-to-working/protection, manual-to-working/protection, sf-on-working, sd-on-protection, wait-to-restore, protection-lockout, frozen and so on (default unavailable), plus last-switch-trigger, remaining-wtr and switch-failure-reason. Switch behaviour is configured on protection-group: switching-mode unidirectional (default) or bidirectional, reversion-mode revertive|non-revertive (default non-revertive), hold-off-timer 0..10000 ms in 1 ms steps (default 0), wtr-timer 60..720 s (default 300, revertive only), and the triggers client-side-olos-trigger, client-side-sd-trigger, network-side-csf-trigger and network-side-sd-trigger, all disabled by default. Operate it with protection-switch [-f] operation-type=force|lockout|manual|release switch-target= protection-group=, or set pg-request.

Trigger it with verify [-f] fiber-connection [target-select=]<port-id> [allow-switching]; if the port-id is omitted, all paths are verified, and if the port takes part in several CableID paths, all of them are included. allow-switching is false by default, which checks active paths only; true lets the system initiate OPSM switching so working and protection paths are both verified. Pre-condition: equipment-policies cable-id-control must be enabled. On acceptance the NE raises CID-verification-in-progress and the command returns immediately. Watch it with show cable-id-status: cable-id-state idle|running-incl-switching|running-no-switching and test-progress as N out of M completed. Results per port pair are in show [-r] cable-id-path-<name>: card-type-a/port-a and card-type-z/port-z (CAD10A or RD20TM), port-a-to-port-z-last-test-status and the reverse, not-verified|pass|fail, the path-status fields, last-test-qualifier up-to-date|out-dated, last-test-timestamp and additional-info (Cable-ID-MISMATCH, Cable-ID TxLOS, Cable-ID RxLOS, Cable-ID-RxLOF, power out-of-range, timeout). terminate cable-id stops running tests.

Where authentication is sent is decided by security-policies aaa-authentication-method: local-only (the default, in which case the node never contacts RADIUS at all), local-first-then-remote, remote-first-then-local, or remote-unavailable-then-local. Authorization has its own policy, aaa-authorization-method, also local-only by default; changing it requires the user to log out and back in. The target itself is aaa-server-<server-name>: protocol-supported RADIUS (default) or TACACSPLUS, server-address, server-priority 1-10 (lowest number is highest precedence), enabled default true, shared-secret default sharedkey with a 64 character maximum, server-port-authentication default 1812, server-port-accounting default 1813, server-port default 49, source-ip and role-supported authentication/authorization/accounting. What happens when it does not answer is governed by timeout, 1..90 seconds default 5, and retry, 0..5 with a default of 3; total wait, timeout x (retry + 1), should stay under 5 minutes. TACACS+ counters are visible with show aaa-statistics.

The automation account's public key goes in ssh-authorized-key: add ssh-authorized-key-<user-name>/<key-id> public-key <value> [label <value>]. Each entry holds a trusted public key for SSHv2 user authentication, for a local or remote user; user-name 0..32, key-id 1..64, public-key up to 2048 characters in OpenSSH/PEM form, with public-key-algorithm ecdsa-sha2-nistp256/384/521 or ssh-rsa2048/3072/4096. Also set security-policies ssh-authentication-method to public-key or public-key-or-password, since the default is password. The remote host the node copies files to goes in ssh-known-host: add ssh-known-host-<id> address <hostname/IPv4/IPv6> public-key-algorithm <value> public-key <value>, which additionally accepts ssh-ed25519 (from R9.0). How strictly that identity is enforced is security-policies ssh-strict-host-key-checking, strict or relaxed (default relaxed). The node's own keys are separate: show ssh-host-key-<public-key-algorithm> lists the global host keys (one per algorithm, auto-generated in the default DB), and ssh-keygen [-b=<len>] [-t=rsa|ecdsa|ed25519] [-l=<label>] regenerates them.

The key agreement policy is mka-policy, referenced by the macsec entity of the Ethernet facility: add/set mka-policy-<name> [key-server-priority] [macsec-cipher-suite] [confidentiality-offset] [sak-rekey-interval]. key-server-priority is what MKA uses to elect the key server, macsec-cipher-suite is the cipher suite for Secure Association Key derivation, and confidentiality-offset is the number of octets in an Ethernet frame sent as unencrypted plain text. The session key rollover is sak-rekey-interval, the SAK rekey interval in seconds, range 0 or 30..65535, default 30 s. The policy is bound per port through macsec-mka-<name> mka-policy <name>, which also holds connectivity-association-key and connectivity-association-key-name (0..64), psk-lifetime 1..173 days (default 14), psk-expiration-warning, psk-lifetime-enable, and reports is-key-server. Watch the channels with show sc-tx-<name>/<index> and show sc-rx-<name>/<index>: sci-tx or sci-rx as a 16 character hex string, state in-use or not-in-use, association-number, key-identifier and next-packet-number.

netconf: enabled true by default and it cannot be disabled from within a NETCONF session; port is the SSH listening port, range 1..65535, default 830; hello-timeout 1..3600 seconds, default 2; annotate-cli-name false; static-info-in-notifs up to 10 YANG identifiers. grpc, which carries gNMI: enabled true by default, port default 50051, gnmi-get-encoding-granularity per-path or per-object with per-object as the default. restconf: enabled true by default and https-enabled true with https-port 1..65535 default 8181, but http-enabled is false out of the box (RESTCONF HTTP access is not supported in secure mode) with http-port default 8080, and cookie-timeout 1..300 minutes default 5. So the only thing off by default is RESTCONF over plain HTTP. For comparison the CLI protocol itself listens over ssh on cli port 22 with enabled true.

restart [-h] [-f] [<resource-id>] [<type>] [<sub-component>] defaults to a warm restart if type is not given, and restarts the active node controller card if no resource-id is given. warm reboots the processor of the card (CHM6, UCM4 and similar) and is non service affecting, with connectivity back within five minutes, though on XMM4 visibility is lost for about 3 minutes. cold reboots all components and sub-components and is service affecting, again with connectivity regained within five minutes, but a cold reboot of XMM4 is not service affecting and only loses visibility. shutdown gracefully shuts the card down. No, you cannot assume uniform behaviour: the guide states explicitly that not all cards support all restart types. Restartable entities are card (cold, warm, shutdown), a card sub-component (cold, warm; list them with show card resources) and tom (cold only). The command asks for confirmation unless -f is supplied.

Three things. First a template per TOM part-number: add serdes-template-<name> [tom-part-number <value>] [card-types-applicable <value>] [ports-applicable <value>], where ports-applicable is all by default, or up to 20 named ports such as T1 or T10. Second the parameter values inside it: add serdes-template-entry-<serdes-template-name>/<entry-name> value <value>, for example RxAmplitude, RxEQ, RxPreCursor, RxPostCursor, TxEQ, TxEQAdaptive. Third the global switch: set equipment-templates use-serdes-templates true, which is disabled by default; on enabling, templates are not applied retroactively, only from that moment onward. Templates apply to all line cards that support serdes (see supported-card support-serdes-config). When a TOM with that part-number is plugged in, the template is applied automatically; swapping in a TOM with a different part-number resets the serdes configuration and re-applies the new template if one exists. Manual serdes settings are kept even where they deviate from the template, and apply-template forces re-application.

ots, the Optical Transport Section, is the fiber span: fiber-type-tx/rx, fiber-length-tx/rx, span-loss-reference with span-loss-transmit/receive and span-loss-derived values, external-attenuation-tx/rx, raman-coefficient-tx/rx, target-power-setting, loading-policy, osc-less (default disabled, for interworking with systems having no compatible OSC or spans outside the OSC budget) and the read-only laser-safety-mode, OPLM (Optical Power Limited Mode, default) or APSD (Automatic Power Shut Down). oms, the Optical Multiplex Section, is the multiplexed spectrum: band-allowed/band-actual/band-target, grid-mode (flexible, fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-100G-48ch and others), configured-spectrum, target-output-power, attenuation-control-mode-rx/tx; MCs and NMCs hang off it. ops, the Optical Physical Section, is the port-level section carrying role tributary, multi-carrier, active-multi-carrier, general-purpose or ase-input, plus input-psd-profile and port-expansion no|y-cable. osc, the Optical Supervisory Channel, carries the supervisory traffic: osc-mode OC3 (155 Mbit/s) or 1GE with FEC (HSC OLS only), osc-wavelength, l0-comm-interface-type ipv4 or ipv6, osc-control auto|manual.

That behaviour is trib-ptp tributary-disable-action, which defines what the NE does towards the client equipment connected over the TOM when a line-side failure is observed. The default is laser-shut-off; the other values are none, odu-ais, send-ais-1, send-gais, send-idles, send-lf, send-ms-ais and send-nos (1830 GX G30 only). Delay it with tributary-disable-holdoff-timer, range 0..10000 milliseconds, default 0 which disables the hold-off; the guide notes this timer applies when the TDA action is laser turn-off, so the optical signal is held until the timer expires before the laser is turned off. Related switches on the same object: near-end-tda enabled|disabled (default disabled), tda-degrade-mode enabled|disabled (default disabled, BERSD-ODU triggering ALS) and forward-defect-trigger true|false (default true), which decides whether a received client forward defect such as LF or ODU-AIS flows through to the line side or triggers an egress TDA action. Example: set trib-ptp-1-5-T2 tributary-disable-action laser-shut-off.
